rationale: Resolve the open question recorded as a limitation of the previous interpretation: whether the 'leadership transfer in progress' error seen on an explicit transfer to a demoted member belongs to the request itself or to a transfer that was already running when it arrived. This harness runs the same demote-then-transfer setup twice, samples the leader's leadership-transfer flag before the call, immediately after the call returns its future, after the future completes and after a short settle, and issues exactly one request in the first case and the earlier five-attempt sequence in the second while sampling the flag before every attempt. If the flag is clear before the first request and the future still reports an in-progress error, that error belongs to the request; if the flag is already set, the earlier receipt's error is explained by a prior transfer and the target was never attempted.

scope.description: Two cases on separate four-member clusters with one demoted follower each: a single explicit transfer to the demoted member with the leader's transfer flag sampled around the call, and the five-attempt retry sequence with the flag sampled before every attempt.
assumptions: The demoted member is a follower at demotion time, chosen as any member other than the sitting leader.
Each case bootstraps its own cluster, so the two cases share no state.
The harness waits up to two seconds for the demoted member's own GetConfiguration to report the non-voter role and records whether it converged.
The transfer flag is read through the package-internal accessor on the node that is leader at the moment of the call, so the sample describes the node the request is sent to.
excluded: No assertion about client-write availability after the transfer; that was measured in the previous receipt.
Only explicit transfers are issued; the automatic form is covered by the earlier control.
Leadership is sampled every ten milliseconds from each member's State, so a shorter leaderless interval can be missed.

experiment.prefix: Each case bootstraps a four-peer in-memory cluster, waits for a leader, demotes a non-leader member with DemoteVoter, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until it reports the non-voter role. A case event records the demoted member, its role view, convergence time and the leader before the transfer. The single case samples getLeadershipTransferInProgress on the leader, calls LeadershipTransferToServer once, samples the flag again as soon as the future is returned, awaits the future for at most five seconds, samples the flag after completion and again after three hundred milliseconds. The retry case reproduces the five-attempt loop, sampling the flag before each attempt and recording each attempt's error, retrying only while the error names a transfer already in progress. Both result events record the future outcome, the flag samples, whether the named member ever reported Leader during a three-second sample, the leaderless sample count and the final leader.
experiment.responsibility: LeadershipTransferToServer accepts a caller-named member and is documented as transferring leadership to that server; the library owns both the target check and the bookkeeping that decides whether a transfer is already running. An in-progress error returned for a request that was issued while no transfer was running would attribute the failure to that request, while one returned because an earlier transfer was still active would mean the named target was never attempted at all.

comparisons.description: A single explicit transfer to a configured member must install that member if it is accepted; a false witness contradicts it.

The first request must be issued while no transfer is running, so that any in-progress error belongs to that request rather than to an earlier one; a true witness would instead explain the earlier receipt as a prior stalled transfer.

knowledge.assertion: An explicit transfer target is resolved only through leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters, while pickServer skips non-voters.
A voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting a configured non-voter candidate, and timeoutNow forces candidacy without checking suffrage or term.
